lines.speaker: Codex
lines.text: Year 2060. No true copy of the text survives. You are a scribe, sent to see it with your own eyes and record it faithfully. Watch, listen, and write.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.

beats.title: Days Two and Three: Sky, Sea, and Land

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.

beats.title: Days Four and Five: Lights, Birds, and Fish

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it was so.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the LORD God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: God put the man in the garden to dress it and to keep it. A river waters this garden. Help tend it: fill your jar at the river, then water each thirsty plant.

done.speaker: Scripture
done.text: And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.

done.speaker: Scribe
done.text: Scribe's note: work was part of God's good plan from the very start. Adam was given the garden to care for.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field, and every fowl of the air; and brought them unto Adam to see what he would call them: and whatsoever Adam called every living creature, that was the name thereof.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: God is bringing each creature to Adam. As Adam names them, write each one in your scroll under the groups Scripture uses. Walk up gently, or they'll startle.

after_lines.speaker: Scripture
after_lines.text: And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof;

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And they were both naked, the man and his wife, and were not ashamed.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Remember God's words: of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat. Gather fruit from the trees that sparkle. The one tree God forbade stands just ahead, and its fruit is not for gathering.

done.speaker: Scribe
done.text: Scribe's note: so much was given freely. Only one tree was held back, and God told them why (Genesis 2:17).

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: They are hiding somewhere among the trees. Look for the rustling leaves to see where they are.

after_lines.speaker: Scripture
after_lines.text: And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.

after_lines.speaker: Scripture
after_lines.text: And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?

after_lines.speaker: Scripture
after_lines.text: And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.

after_lines.speaker: Scripture
after_lines.text: And the LORD God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

after_lines.speaker: Scripture
after_lines.text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.

after_lines.speaker: Scripture
after_lines.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Before you travel on, check your scroll. Fill in the missing words from what you recorded.

questions.text: And God said, Let there be ____: and there was ____.
questions.full: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

questions.text: And on the ____ day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested.
questions.full: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.

questions.text: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to ____ it and to keep it.
questions.full: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

questions.text: And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every ____ of the field.
questions.full: And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.

questions.text: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, ____
questions.full: And the LORD God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?

after_lines.speaker: Codex
after_lines.text: You have recorded all of it, word for word. Chapter complete.

discoverables.name: Darkness over the deep
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: Genesis 1:2 says the earth was without form and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep. Creation begins from nothing but God's word.

discoverables.name: Evening and morning
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: each day in Genesis 1 ends 'the evening and the morning', so the Hebrew day begins at evening. You'll see this pattern every day of creation.

discoverables.name: Waters gathered
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: God names the dry land Earth and the gathered waters Seas, and sees that it is good (Genesis 1:10).

discoverables.name: Seed-bearing plants
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: plants reproduce 'after his kind'. This phrase repeats through the chapter and describes the order God set in creation.

discoverables.name: Sun, moon, and stars
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: on the fourth day the lights are set for signs, seasons, days, and years, so they mark time and guide travelers (Genesis 1:14-18).

discoverables.name: Fish and birds
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: on the fifth day God blesses the sea creatures and birds, saying 'Be fruitful, and multiply' (Genesis 1:22).

discoverables.name: Dominion
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: man and woman are given care over the creatures of land, sea, and air (Genesis 1:28).

discoverables.name: A day set apart
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: God blessed and sanctified the seventh day (Genesis 2:3). It becomes the pattern for the Sabbath in later Scripture.

discoverables.name: Tree of life
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: two trees stand in the midst of the garden: the tree of life and the tree of knowledge of good and evil (Genesis 2:9).

discoverables.name: The river of Eden
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: Genesis 2:10 describes a river going out of Eden to water the garden and then dividing into four heads.

discoverables.name: Garden tools
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: Adam was put in the garden to dress it and to keep it (Genesis 2:15). Work existed before the fall.

discoverables.name: Animals brought to Adam
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: God brings the animals to Adam to see what he would call them. Adam names them all, but finds no companion like himself.

discoverables.name: Marriage
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: Genesis 2:24 says a man shall leave his father and mother and cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.

discoverables.name: The forbidden tree
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: this is the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Of every other tree they may freely eat, but of this one God said, thou shalt not eat of it (Genesis 2:17).

discoverables.name: Fig leaves
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: after eating, Adam and Eve sew fig leaves into aprons (Genesis 3:7).

discoverables.name: Eve named
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: Adam calls his wife Eve, because she was the mother of all living (Genesis 3:20).

discoverables.name: Cherubim and a flaming sword
discoverables.note: Scribe's note: God places cherubim and a flaming sword at the east of Eden to keep the way of the tree of life (Genesis 3:24).

forbidden_fruit.speaker: Adam
forbidden_fruit.text: Don't you know you are not to eat from that tree?

forbidden_fruit.speaker: Adam
forbidden_fruit.text: Not that one! The LORD God said of this tree, thou shalt not eat of it.

forbidden_fruit.speaker: Adam
forbidden_fruit.text: Again? Every other tree in the whole garden is yours to enjoy. Just not this one!

forbidden_fruit.speaker: Adam
forbidden_fruit.text: Put it down, friend. That is the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

forbidden_fruit.speaker: Adam
forbidden_fruit.text: Don't you know you are not to eat from that tree? I'll keep knocking it away as long as it takes.

forbidden_fruit.speaker: Adam
forbidden_fruit.text: You are a stubborn one! Try the figs over there, they are very good.

side_quests.title: Seeds after his kind
side_quests.task: Gather seeds from the new plants

intro.speaker: Scribe
intro.text: The dry land is already full of plants, and every one carries its own seed. I'd like to gather a few for my scroll.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Find five seed pods on the new land. Look for the green sparkles.

done.speaker: Scripture
done.text: And the earth brought forth grass, and herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed was in itself, after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

done.speaker: Scribe
done.text: Scribe's note: each plant makes seed after its own kind. God built the whole garden to keep on growing.

intro.speaker: Scribe
intro.text: Birds! The very first ones. A few have landed on the rocks to rest.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Walk up to four perched birds and sketch each one in your scroll.

done.speaker: Scripture
done.text: And God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

intro.speaker: Scribe
intro.text: Listen... a little bleat, far off. One lamb has wandered away from the flock.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Find the lost lamb, call it, and lead it back to the sheep on the other side of the path.

done.speaker: Scripture
done.text: And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

done.speaker: Scribe
done.text: Scribe's note: back with its flock. Later Scripture often calls God's people His sheep.

intro.speaker: Scribe
intro.text: Everything is finished, and God is resting. Maybe a scribe can rest a moment too.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Sit on the mossy stone and rest for a few moments.

done.speaker: Scripture
done.text: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.

done.speaker: Scribe
done.text: Scribe's note: rest was part of creation too. God blessed the seventh day and made it holy.

side_quests.title: The four heads of the river
side_quests.task: Find the four springs of the river

intro.speaker: Scribe
intro.text: Scripture says the river out of Eden parts into four heads. Each one has a name.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Follow the river and find four springs along its bank, up the screen. Record each name.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: The name of the first is Pison: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia.

lines.speaker: Scripture
lines.text: And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth toward the east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates.

lines.speaker: Scribe
lines.text: The fourth head is Euphrates, named last in Genesis 2:14. People still know that river's name in 2060.

done.speaker: Scribe
done.text: Scribe's note: four rivers from one. The Euphrates and the Tigris (Hiddekel) are rivers people still know today.

intro.speaker: Scribe
intro.text: Something glints in the stream by the pond. Scripture mentions treasures in the land around the river.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Find three treasures: gold in the stream, bdellium by the pond, and onyx on the riverbank.

lines.speaker: Scribe
lines.text: Gold, shining in the stream.

lines.speaker: Scribe
lines.text: Bdellium: a pale, sweet-smelling resin, like a pearl of tree sap.

lines.speaker: Scribe
lines.text: And the onyx stone, black with bands of white.

done.speaker: Scripture
done.text: And the gold of that land is good: there is bdellium and the onyx stone.

done.speaker: Scribe
done.text: Scribe's note: onyx shows up again much later, on the shoulders of the high priest's clothes (Exodus 28:9).

side_quests.title: Green herb for every beast
side_quests.deliver_task: Give a herb to three animals

deliver_intro.speaker: Codex
deliver_intro.text: Now give one herb each to three different animals. Walk up to one and tap to share.

intro.speaker: Scribe
intro.text: Scripture says God gave the green plants as food for every beast. The animals here look hungry!

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Pick three green herbs, then share them with three different animals.

done.speaker: Scripture
done.text: And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.

deliver_intro.speaker: Codex
deliver_intro.text: A lovely bunch. Now bring them to Eve.

intro.speaker: Scribe
intro.text: Eve is seeing the garden for the very first time. I'll pick her some of the best flowers.

intro.speaker: Codex
intro.text: Pick five sparkling flowers, then bring them to Eve.

done.speaker: Eve
done.text: For me? They are beautiful! Everything in this garden is so good.

done.speaker: Scripture
done.text: And out of the ground made the LORD God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.

lines.speaker: Codex
lines.text: Chapter 1 is restored and safe in your scroll. The time gate is open again, just past the cherubim.

lines.speaker: Scribe
lines.text: Adam and Eve have a long road ahead of them. Let's see what happens to their family.

lines.speaker: Codex
lines.text: Step into the time gate when you're ready. Next: Genesis 4, Cain and Abel.
